text: Annette Leslie Jones (born September 7, 1967) is an American stand-up comedian and actress. She was a cast member and writer for the NBC sketch comedy series Saturday Night Live from 2014 to 2019, and hosted the ABC game show Supermarket Sweep. She has also performed as a featured act at the Just for Laughs festival in Montreal and the Aspen Comedy Festival. In 2010, her one-hour comedy special, Problem Child, aired on Showtime. Jones starred in Ghostbusters (2016) as Patty Tolan. In 2017 and 2018, she was nominated for a Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Supporting Actress in a Comedy Series for her work on Saturday Night Live. Born in Memphis, Tennessee, Jones has a younger brother, Rodney Keith Jones (1971–2009). Her father, Willie Jones Jr., served in the U.S. Army, and the family moved frequently. They relocated to Los Angeles when her father took a job at Stevie Wonder's radio station, KJLH, as an electronics engineer. Jones attended high school in Lynwood, California, where she played basketball, a sport her father encouraged due to her height. She earned a basketball scholarship to Chapman University, where she worked as a disc jockey at KNAB and considered playing professional basketball overseas. When her coach, Brian Berger, left Chapman in 1986 for Colorado State University, Jones followed. At Colorado State, she considered a pre-law degree but switched majors to accounting and computer science before settling on communications. Jones began stand-up comedy in college in 1987 after winning a "Funniest Person on Campus" contest. After winning, she left school to move to Los Angeles, where she performed at comedy clubs while working at Roscoe's House of Chicken and Waffles and UPS. Comedians Mother Love and Dave Chappelle encouraged her to move to New York City, where she lived for over two years and appeared on BET's ComicView before returning to Los Angeles. She performed at The Comedy Store in West Hollywood, but her shows received negative reviews. She then went on tour, opening for Jamie Foxx, where she was booed; Foxx advised her to "live life for a little while," and she stopped performing for three years. She performed in smaller clubs until 2010, when she began requesting spots at The Comedy Store and secured prime-time slots. In 2012, Chris Rock saw her perform and introduced her to several top comedy managers, all of whom did not recognize her potential. The following year, Rock helped her secure an audition for Saturday Night Live, which she landed. In 2008, Jones participated in Katt Williams's It's Pimpin' Pimpin' tour. Netflix signed her for a stand-up special scheduled for 2020. In December 2013, SNL held a casting call to add at least one African American woman, and Jones auditioned. Before the audition, she criticized the show and Kenan Thompson, calling it "not funny." Sasheer Zamata was added as a featured player, while Jones and LaKendra Tookes were hired as writers. Jones appeared in the Weekend Update segment of the May 3, 2014 episode hosted by Andrew Garfield, where her jokes about dating and being a breeding slave caused controversy. She appeared in the first and third episodes of the 40th season, hosted by Chris Pratt and Bill Hader, respectively. On October 20, 2014, Jones was promoted to cast as a featured player and made her official debut on the October 25, 2014 episode hosted by Jim Carrey. At age 47, she became the oldest person to join SNL as a cast member, surpassing Michael McKean and George Coe, who joined at 46 in 1994 and 1975. Her addition marked the first time in SNL history that the cast included more than one African American woman; the 40th season also became the first to have five concurrent African American cast members, breaking the previous record of three. Jones returned for Seasons 41, 42 (where she was promoted to Repertory Status), 43, and 44. The 44th season was her final season on SNL. In 2006, Jones appeared in Master P's film Repos. In 2014, she appeared in Chris Rock's directorial film, Top Five; Rock later said a follow-up was in development, stating, "Some people really shine in Top Five. You might want to see a little more Leslie Jones." In 2015, she appeared in the Judd Apatow and Amy Schumer project, Trainwreck; Apatow and Schumer wrote a role specifically for her after seeing her in Top Five. In 2016, she starred in the Ghostbusters reboot as Patty Tolan, alongside Melissa McCarthy, Kristen Wiig, and Kate McKinnon. She also appeared in Coming 2 America with Tracy Morgan, Rick Ross, and KiKi Layne. Since 2017, she has been a member of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences in the Actors Branch. During the 2016 Summer Olympics in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, Jones regularly live-tweeted events and posted reaction videos. Her commentary gained popularity, with articles such as The Huffington Post's "Watching Leslie Jones Watch The Olympics Is Better Than the Actual Olympics" highlighting her enthusiasm. Television producer Mike Shoemaker, a follower, suggested to NBC executive producer Jim Bell that Jones join the Olympics coverage team; Bell responded by asking her to join, and she accepted, covering swimming, track and field, gymnastics, and beach volleyball. Jones reprised her role at the 2018 Winter Olympics in South Korea and live-tweeted for the postponed 2020 Summer Olympics in Tokyo, Japan. She live-tweeted for the final time at the 2022 Winter Olympics in Beijing, China, and released a statement on Twitter saying this would be her last Olympics live-tweet, claiming NBC was pressuring her to stop. Jones and comedian Adam DeVine appeared in a 2016 Allstate Insurance ad campaign created by Leo Burnett Worldwide. In 2017, she hosted the BET Awards, marking her hosting debut. In 2018, she appeared in two advertisements for Amazon's Echo Spot. In 2020, she hosted a Supermarket Sweep reboot and returned for season 2 in 2021. She also hosted the 2021 MTV Movie & TV Awards. Jones has cited Eddie Murphy, Richard Pryor, Carol Burnett, Lucille Ball, John Ritter, and Whoopi Goldberg as her comedic influences. She is a fan of the Seattle Sounders FC and RuPaul's Drag Race. After the release of Ghostbusters in July 2016, Jones faced racist and misogynistic attacks on Twitter. The platform took action, permanently banning user and Breitbart editor Milo Yiannopoulos, who called her "barely literate." Jones temporarily left Twitter on July 18, 2016. She appeared on Late Night with Seth Meyers to discuss the incident and her meeting with Twitter CEO Jack Dorsey, where she stated that "hate speech and freedom of speech are two different things." A month later, her personal website was hacked, with its content replaced by photos of her passport and driver's license—an instance of doxxing—and alleged nude images, along with a video tribute to Harambe, the Cincinnati Zoo gorilla killed in May 2016, a reference to the racist remarks made about her. Her team took the site down immediately. Both incidents sparked widespread support from fans and celebrities using the hashtag #LoveForLeslieJ, which trended on Twitter and Instagram. Supporters included Paul Feig, Gabourey Sidibe, Ellen DeGeneres, Sara Benincasa, Ava DuVernay, Hillary Clinton, Corey Taylor, Katy Perry, Octavia Spencer, Anna Kendrick, Lena Dunham, and Loni Love. Jones addressed the hacks on the October 22, 2016 episode of Saturday Night Live. When she appeared on Late Night with Seth Meyers on May 12, 2015, a montage of fans showed their support for her.
